name: 倒楼滩
Upturned Tower Strand
before: 雾在身后合上了。后千里驶出雾海的头一个清早，海面平得像一张纸，东边天上浮着一排楼台，层层叠叠，檐角朝下，倒挂在半空。船朝它驶了一整天，它不近也不远。傍晚靠上一片白滩，滩上站着一队披旧甲的蜃兵，甲片在夕阳里一闪一闪，像隔着一层水；兵阵后头还有几个海盗，脚下踩出了实实在在的脚印。

The fog closes behind you. On Houqianli's first morning out of the Sea of Fog the water lies flat as a sheet of paper, and in the eastern sky floats a row of towers, tier on tier, eaves pointing down, hanging upside down in mid-air. The ship sails at them all day and they come no nearer and drift no farther. At dusk you put in at a white strand. On it stands a squad of mirage soldiers in old armour whose plates flicker in the sunset as if seen through water; behind their line are a few pirates, and their boots leave honest prints in the sand.
after: 刀砍上去，蜃兵像热气一样散了，只有海盗被捆成了一串。他们说蜃兵是蜃王吐出来的，打散了明早还有，他们只是跟在后头捡便宜。阿舟望着天上的楼，把沈渡那句话又念了一遍：「我在蜃楼等。」小桨趴在滩上听了半天：「地底下有东西在喘气，很慢，很大。」

Blades go through the mirage soldiers and they scatter like heat haze; only the pirates end up tied in a row. They say the soldiers are breathed out by the Mirage King: scatter them and there'll be more tomorrow morning, and the pirates just follow along to pick up what falls. A Zhou looks up at the towers and says Shen Du's words once more: 'I'll be waiting in the Mirage.' Xiaojiang lies with an ear to the sand for a long while. 'Something under here is breathing. Very slow. Very big.'

name: 敲盐坪
Knock-Salt Flat
before: 盐滩上一片白，几十个盐工拿木耙把卤水推成方格，晒成盐。一伙海盗占了盐坪，夹着一队蜃兵督工，晒出的盐全装上他们的船。有个八九岁的丫头拎着一把木盐勺，挨个敲人：敲盐工，「咚」；敲海盗，「咚」；敲到一个蜃兵，勺子从他身上穿了过去。她点点头，在小本子上记了一笔：「假的。」

The salt flat is white from edge to edge, and dozens of salt workers push brine into squares with wooden rakes to dry. A band of pirates has taken the flat, with a squad of mirage soldiers to drive the work, and every grain goes onto their boats. A girl of eight or nine walks among them with a wooden salt spoon, knocking on people. A salt worker: knock. A pirate: knock. A mirage soldier: the spoon goes straight through him. She nods and writes in a little book: 'Not real.'
after: 海盗跑了，蜃兵散了。丫头叫卤妹，小本子叫「真假簿」：在蜃楼底下长大，她分不清哪些是真的，就挨个敲，敲得响的记「真」。她也敲了敲你们，记下：「后千里，真。」簿子头一页写着她爹卤大：「三年前往白城去了，未回。真。」

The pirates run and the soldiers scatter. The girl is called Lumei, and the book is her Real-or-Not Book. Growing up under the Mirage, she can't tell what's real, so she knocks on everything and writes 'real' for what knocks back. She knocks on you too: 'Houqianli: real.' The first page is about her father, Luda: 'Went to the White City three years ago. Not back. Real.'

name: 渴湖滩
Thirst Lake Flats
before: 往东的路上，前头总有一片湖，水亮汪汪地映着天，可走一里，湖退一里。一伙披白麻的蜃母教徒守在路口，给过路人发空水囊：「蜃母赐水，前头就是，不必带。」不少人信了，空着水囊往湖走，走到口干舌燥倒在地上，教徒再去收他们的包袱。今天他们拦住了卤妹，说她爹也是蜃母收走的。

On the road east there is always a lake ahead, bright water mirroring the sky, and for every mile you walk it backs away a mile. A band of Mirage Mother believers in white hemp hold the crossroads, handing travellers empty waterskins: 'The Mother gives water. It's just ahead, no need to carry any.' Plenty believe them and walk toward the lake with empty skins until they drop with parched throats, and then the believers go and collect their bundles. Today they've stopped Lumei, and they tell her the Mother took her father too.
after: 教徒们败了，卤妹抱着空水囊直哼哼。阿汐指着那片湖：「地面晒得滚烫，贴地那一层空气更热、更稀，天光斜照下来，被它往上一折。你看见的『水』，是一块天。」教徒的簿子上写着「卤大，献蜃母」。卤妹一笔划掉：「他不信这个。假的。」

The believers are beaten, and Lumei hugs an empty waterskin and grumbles. Axi points at the lake. 'The ground's baking, so the air right against it is hotter and thinner. Light coming slantwise from the sky gets bent back upward by it. That "water" is a patch of sky.' In the believers' register: 'Luda, given to the Mother.' Lumei strikes it out. 'He didn't believe in that. Not real.'

name: 空蹄原
Empty Hoof Plain
before: 荒原上一队蜃骑朝你们冲过来，马蹄翻飞，尘土滚滚，冲了一顿饭的工夫，还在原地那么远。真正扑上来的是躲在蜃骑尘影里的一伙盗马盐寇，骑着瘦马，放冷箭，箭箭从幻影里钻出来。卤妹蹲下摸了摸地：「蹄声在脚底下，远着呢。近的是那几匹瘦的。」

A troop of mirage riders charges at you across the plain, hooves flying, dust rolling, and after the time it takes to eat a meal they are still exactly as far away. What actually falls on you is a gang of horse-thieving salt bandits on scrawny mounts, hiding in the phantom dust and loosing arrows that come out of the image. Lumei crouches and feels the ground. 'The hoofbeats under my hand are far off. The close ones are those skinny horses.'
after: 盐寇被打散了。他们说那队骑兵天天冲，从没冲到过，大概真有一营人在很远的地方操练。卤妹翻开真假簿，在她爹那一页旁边抄上他常说的一句话：「看见的东西都在，只是不在那儿。」她头一回觉得，这句话不是哄她的。

The bandits scatter. They say that troop charges every day and has never arrived; there's probably a real camp drilling somewhere a long way off. Lumei opens her book and, beside her father's page, copies out something he used to say: 'Everything you see is there. Just not where it looks.' For the first time she thinks he wasn't only saying it to soothe her.

name: 千画屋
House of a Thousand Paintings
before: 荒原上一间土屋，墙上、梁上、门板上全是画，画的都是天上那座白城。画师是个老秀才，每天清早白城一出来，他就画一张，画了十一年，没有两张一样。一伙盐枭闯进屋，说这些画是「藏宝图」，要成捆搬走。老秀才扑在画上：「这画的是天！天上哪来的宝！」

A mud house on the plain, its walls, beams and door panels covered in paintings, all of the White City in the sky. The painter is an old scholar who paints one every morning when the city appears; eleven years of it, and no two alike. A gang of salt smugglers barges in, calling the paintings treasure maps, and starts carrying them off in bundles. The old man throws himself across them. 'These are paintings of the sky! What treasure is there in the sky?'
after: 盐枭被赶走了。卤妹一张张翻画，忽然叫起来：近两年的画里，白城最高那座塔顶上多了个小人，扛着盐耙，每一张都在挥手。老秀才也纳闷过：「楼是死的，人是活的。活人上了画，那就是真有人站在那儿。」

The smugglers are driven off. Lumei leafs through the paintings one by one and suddenly cries out: in the last two years' work, on top of the White City's tallest tower, there's a tiny figure with a salt rake on his shoulder, waving in every single picture. The old man has puzzled over it too. 'Towers don't move. People do. If a living man turns up in the picture, then somebody really is standing there.'

name: 盐课卡
Salt Tax Barrier
before: 路口一座税卡，几个盐课税丁捧着簿子挨个收税：你挑的盐要收，你车上的盐要收，天上蜃楼里那几座盐仓，也按「过目」收，看一眼十文。过路的盐工捂着眼睛走，还是被逮住，说你从指头缝里看见了。卡后头蹲着一队蜃弓手，替税丁压阵。

A tax barrier at the crossroads, where salt-tax men with ledgers collect from everyone: on the salt you carry, on the salt in your cart, and on the salt barns in the Mirage up in the sky, charged 'by sight', ten coppers a look. Salt workers walk past with hands over their eyes and still get caught: you saw it through your fingers. Behind the barrier crouches a squad of mirage archers to back the tax men up.
after: 税丁抱头，卡子拆了。翻他们的税簿，三年前有一行：「东卤场，卤大，缴盐税二斗。」卤妹拿勺子敲了敲那一页：「真的税，就有真的盐场。」税丁小声说，东卤场在三天路外的海边，天上的白城，就挂在那个方向。

The tax men cover their heads and the barrier comes down. In their tax book, three years back, is a line: 'East Brine Works, Luda, salt tax paid, two dou.' Lumei taps the page with her spoon. 'A real tax means a real salt works.' A tax man mutters that the East Brine Works is three days off on the coast, in the very direction where the White City hangs in the sky.

name: 霍家赌棚
Huo's Betting Tent
before: 盐滩当中搭着一座大棚，棚里人声鼎沸，是盐枭霍白眉开的赌场，赌的是蜃楼：今天天上出几座楼，楼是正是倒，日头偏西前散不散。押错的人把盐、船，甚至女儿都押了进去。棚外几十个盐枭夹着蜃兵守着，不赌的不许过路。

In the middle of the salt flat stands a great roaring tent: the gambling house of the salt smuggler Huo Baimei, where the bets are on the Mirage. How many towers today, right way up or upside down, gone before the sun turns west or not. Losers have staked salt, boats, even daughters. Dozens of smugglers and mirage soldiers guard the tent, and no one who won't bet may pass.
after: 盐枭散了，霍白眉只好认账：三年前卤大在这儿押过一注大的，「白城是真的，我走过去给你们看」，押的是他的盐耙。他一走没回来报，霍就把耙挂在墙上当了赢头。卤妹摘下耙，耙柄上刻着她的名字。霍白眉挠挠头：「这一注，我倒是盼着输。」

The smugglers scatter and Huo Baimei has to own up. Three years ago Luda placed a big bet here: 'The White City is real, and I'll walk there to show you.' His stake was his salt rake. He went and never came back to report, so Huo hung the rake on the wall as his winnings. Lumei takes it down; her name is carved in the handle. Huo scratches his head. 'That one, I was hoping to lose.'

name: 苇棚哨
Reed Shed Post
before: 盐沼边一溜苇棚，棚顶插着破旗。一伙蜃弓手守在这里，箭射过来时，弓手看着像在两里外，其实就趴在两百步外的苇子里：热气把他们的影子挪远了。过路人照着影子还手，一箭也挨不着。卤妹不看人，盯着苇子：「哪片苇子晃，人就在哪儿。」

A row of reed sheds at the edge of the salt marsh, tattered flags on the roofs. Mirage archers hold the place, and when their arrows come the bowmen look two li off, though they're lying in the reeds two hundred paces away: the shimmer has moved their shapes. Travellers shoot back at the shapes and never hit a thing. Lumei doesn't watch the men, she watches the reeds. 'Wherever the reeds shake, that's where they are.'
after: 弓手一个个被揪出苇子。他们刚劫过一个东边来的盐贩，筐里是一块块按了手印的盐饼。卤妹捧起一块，把自己的手往印子上一比，眼圈红了：交盐要按手印，这个拇指上有道疤，她爹的拇指就有。「盐是新的，他还在晒盐。」

The archers are dragged out of the reeds one by one. They had just robbed a salt pedlar from the east, and his basket holds salt cakes stamped with thumbprints. Lumei holds one up, sets her own hand against the print, and her eyes go red: salt is handed in with a thumbprint, and this thumb has a scar across it, just like her father's. 'This salt is new. He's still making salt.'

name: 盐骨船
Salt-Bone Ship
before: 平地上搁着一条大船，离海十几里，船身结满白盐，像裹了一层糖霜，桅杆还立着。一伙海盗拿它当窝，舱里堆着抢来的东西，夜里在甲板上点火，远远看去，真像一条船在陆地上航行。卤妹敲了敲船板：「咚，真的。可船怎么会在这儿？」

A great ship sits on dry land a dozen li from the sea, crusted white with salt like sugar frosting, its mast still standing. A pirate band uses it as a den, the hold piled with loot, and at night they light fires on deck, so from afar it really looks like a ship sailing over land. Lumei knocks on the planking. 'Knock. Real. But how did a ship get here?'
after: 海盗被赶下了船。龚墨斗刮开盐壳看船板：「老船，少说一两百年。」老盐工说，这片盐滩从前是海湾，湾口被沙堵死，太阳一年年晒，水走了，盐留下了，船也搁下了。舱壁上有一行新划的炭字：「往东，三日。卤。」

The pirates are put off the ship. Gong Modou scrapes away the salt crust to look at the planks. 'Old. A hundred, two hundred years at least.' An old salt worker says this flat was once a bay; sand choked its mouth, the sun dried it year after year, the water left, the salt stayed, and so did the ship. On the hold wall, in fresh charcoal: 'East, three days. Lu.'

name: 卤水驿
Brine Post
before: 盐滩上唯一的一座驿站，几间土房围着一口卤池，过路人在这儿歇脚、换鞋、买腌菜。一伙兵痞模样的盐枭占了驿站，把驿娘赶去马棚里住，粮缸、菜坛、草鞋全贴了封条。要歇脚，先交三斗盐；交不出盐，就去卤池里替他们捞盐抵账。

The only post station on the salt flat: a few mud rooms around a brine pool, where travellers rest, change shoes and buy pickles. A gang of smugglers who carry themselves like soldiers has taken it, sent the postmistress to sleep in the stable, and sealed the grain jars, pickle crocks and straw sandals. To rest here you pay three dou of salt; no salt, and you work it off raking their brine pool.
after: 兵痞被撵走，驿娘回到灶前，炉子又冒了烟。她记得三年前卤大在这儿住过一夜，拿盐换了双新鞋，问她白城有多远。她说看着一天路。他说他算过，要三天：「看着近，是光哄人。」

The thugs are thrown out, the postmistress goes back to her stove and smoke rises again. She remembers Luda staying a night three years ago; he traded salt for new shoes and asked how far the White City was. A day, it looks like, she told him. He said he'd worked it out: three days. 'It only looks close because the light is fooling you.'
first: 驿里抄出兵痞囤的十二坛腌萝卜、四十双新草鞋、三袋糙米，还有一口小铁锅，锅底刻着驿娘的名字，是他们头一天就抢走的。

From the post you seize the thugs' hoard: twelve crocks of pickled radish, forty pairs of new straw sandals, three sacks of brown rice, and a small iron pot with the postmistress's name scratched on the bottom, the first thing they took from her.
pass: 每次路过，驿娘都给你们每人一双新编的草鞋，鞋底垫了两层，说盐滩烫脚；再舀一碗腌萝卜：「咸的配咸的，走盐路不口淡。」

Each time you pass, the postmistress gives each of you a pair of newly plaited sandals with double soles, because the salt flat burns your feet, and ladles out a bowl of pickled radish. 'Salt with salt. Walk the salt road and you'll never lack for flavour.'

name: 卤虫湖
Brine Shrimp Lake
before: 小咸水湖边，一个瞎眼的老渔翁拿细纱网捞卤虫：一种指甲大的红虫子，晒干了喂鱼喂鸡。几个海盗抢了他的纱网，嫌卤虫不值钱，拿网去兜湖边的野鸭，网兜破了好几处。老渔翁摸着湖岸一路追：「网还我！我靠它数日子呢！」

On the shore of the little salt lake a blind old fisherman sweeps for brine shrimp with a fine gauze net: red creatures the size of a fingernail, dried to feed fish and hens. A few pirates have taken his net, sneered that shrimp are worthless, and are using it to scoop wild ducks, tearing it in several places. The old man feels his way along the shore after them. 'Give it back! I count my days by it!'
after: 网要回来了。老渔翁说三年前卤大陪他在湖边走过一天，「他拿根竿子插在地上，比着天上的楼脚，说楼脚悬着不沾地，是光拐了弯，拐弯来的东西，比看着远」。说完他侧耳听了听湖面：「他走的时候一路哼歌，哼的是哄小孩睡觉的调子。」

The net is recovered. The old man says that three years ago Luda walked a day along the lake with him. 'He stuck a pole in the ground and sighted the towers' feet against it. The feet hang in the air, he said, so the light has turned a corner, and what comes round a corner is farther than it looks.' Then he turns his ear to the water. 'He hummed all the way when he left. A tune for putting a child to sleep.'

name: 逃丁窝
Runaways' Hollow
before: 盐滩往南是一片沙，沙窝里猫着一伙逃盐丁：从东边盐场逃出来的，在这儿落了草，拦路抢饼抢水，又抢不过谁，饿得前胸贴后背，只好拉了几个蜃兵充门面。他们挥着棍子冲上来，卤妹一眼看见他们的手，喊：「是晒盐的手！别打太狠！」

South of the salt flat lies sand, and in a sandy hollow hides a gang of runaway salt workers: fled from a salt works in the east, turned outlaw, robbing travellers of flatbread and water and losing most of the fights, so starved they've roped in a few mirage soldiers for show. They charge with clubs, and Lumei takes one look at their hands and shouts, 'Those are salt workers' hands! Don't hit too hard!'
after: 逃盐丁扔了棍子，跪在沙里讨吃的。他们认得卤大：东卤场的老把式，管头打人，他挡在前头，背上挨了三鞭。他托他们给女儿捎一只盐雕的小鸟，他们揣了一年，不知道往哪儿送。卤妹接过小鸟，舔了一下：「咸的。真的。」

The runaways drop their clubs and kneel in the sand begging food. They know Luda: an old hand at the East Brine Works who stepped in front when the foreman was beating someone and took three lashes on his back. He asked them to carry a little bird carved from salt to his daughter, and they've carried it a year without knowing where to take it. Lumei takes the bird and licks it. 'Salty. Real.'

name: 镜车阵
Mirror Cart Ring
before: 一队大车从北边过来，车上竖着一面面磨亮的铜镜，太阳一照，满荒原都是光斑。押车的是一伙番人走私客，雇了几个蜃弓手。他们把镜车在盐滩上摆成一圈，照出一座假城楼，骗过路人进「城」投宿；进去的人，就别想带着包袱出来。

A string of big carts rolls in from the north, each with polished bronze mirrors standing upright, scattering light across the plain. The drivers are foreign smugglers who've hired a few mirage archers. They circle the carts on the salt flat so the mirrors throw up a fake city gate and lure travellers in for a night's lodging; whoever goes in won't come out with their bundles.
after: 走私客被打散，镜子一面面放倒，假城没了。头目说这手是跟天上学的：「天上的城，是真城挪了个地方；我们的城，是一堆镜子。」卤妹把这句话抄进簿子，又在旁边添了一句：「爹在的那座城，不是镜子。」

The smugglers scatter, the mirrors are laid flat, and the false city is gone. Their leader says they learned the trick from the sky. 'The city up there is a real city moved somewhere else. Ours is a heap of mirrors.' Lumei copies that into her book and adds beside it: 'The city Dad is in is not mirrors.'

name: 剪绳沼
Rope-Snip Marsh
before: 盐沼里有一片卤水塘，塘边的泥又软又咸，盐工都绕着走：塘里住着一群大青蟹，钳子比人手还大，夜里成群爬上岸，剪鞋子、剪绳子、剪晾着的衣裳。今晚蟹群又上来了，正围着一辆陷在泥里的盐车，咔嚓咔嚓地剪车绳，赶车的老妪拿扁担左扑右打。

In the salt marsh lies a pool of brine with soft, salty mud around it that salt workers always skirt: it's home to a horde of big blue crabs with claws larger than a man's hand, which swarm ashore at night and snip shoes, ropes and laundry on the line. Tonight they're up again, ringing a salt cart stuck in the mud and clacking through its harness ropes while the old woman driving it lays about with her carrying pole.
after: 蟹群被赶回了塘里。老妪是给东卤场送饭的，说卤大是场里的好人，每回发饭都多舀一勺给年纪小的，自己啃锅巴。她指了指东边：「顺着车辙走，三天。去吧，丫头。」卤妹把她的名字记进了簿子，后面写：「真，好人。」

The crabs are driven back into the pool. The old woman carries meals out to the East Brine Works, and she says Luda is a good man there: every time food is handed out he gives the youngest an extra ladle and gnaws the pot scrapings himself. She points east. 'Follow the ruts. Three days. Go on, girl.' Lumei writes her name in the book, and after it: 'Real. Good person.'

name: 看楼碑
Tower-Watch Stele
before: 沙地上立着一块石碑，碑上一个大「风」字，碑脚下一圈刻痕，像一面钟。几个盐枭正要把碑撬倒，说碑底下埋着前朝的盐引。守碑的是个哑巴老汉，死死抱着碑身，手指一个劲地朝天上指，急得脸都紫了。

A stone stele stands in the sand, a great character for 'wind' carved on it and a ring of notches around its foot like a clock face. Some salt smugglers are about to lever it over, saying old salt licences are buried under it. Its keeper, a mute old man, clings to the stone and keeps jabbing a finger at the sky, purple in the face.
after: 盐枭散了。哑巴在沙上画给你们看：哪天早上海面冷、上头的风暖，白城就出得早、出得高；风一乱，楼就碎成一截一截。这块碑是看楼的钟，一圈刻痕记着多少年的楼。卤妹抄下：「白城不骗人，看天出。」

The smugglers scatter. The mute draws it for you in the sand: on mornings when the sea is cold and the air above it warm, the White City comes early and high; when the wind turns rough, the towers break into pieces. The stele is a clock for watching towers, its ring of notches years of sightings. Lumei copies it down: 'The White City doesn't lie. It comes with the weather.'

name: 两请台
Two-Invitation Stage
before: 荒原上一座草台，一个走江湖的小戏班被两拨人堵在台上：一拨是盐枭，一拨是盐课税丁，都要戏班今晚到自家席上唱，谁家晚了就砸谁家的箱子。班主左右作揖，丑角抱着鼓躲在台底下。两拨人吵着吵着动了刀，台板都被踩塌了一块。

A straw-roofed stage on the plain, and a small travelling troupe trapped on it between two crowds: salt smugglers on one side, salt-tax men on the other, each demanding the troupe sing at their feast tonight, and threatening to smash the trunks of whichever comes late. The troupe master bows left and right, the clown hides under the stage with his drum, and as the two sides shout, knives come out and a stage board gives way.
after: 两拨人都被打跑，戏班总算能自己定唱哪出。丑角说三年前一个晒盐的汉子搭他们的车走过一程，夜里帮着演了一回盐神，唱得跑调。问他去哪儿，他说：「我闺女分不清真假，我得走一趟真的，给她看。」卤妹低着头，把这句话一个字一个字抄下来。

Both crowds are driven off, and the troupe can choose its own play at last. The clown says that three years ago a salt worker rode a stretch with them and one night stood in as the Salt God, singing off key. Asked where he was going, he said: 'My girl can't tell real from not. I have to walk to something real, so I can show her.' Lumei bows her head and copies the sentence out, one character at a time.

name: 硬壳道
Hard Crust Road
before: 往东只有一条走得通的路：一线硬盐壳，两边是软泥，一脚下去拔不出来。路口守着一伙雇来的刀客，见人就问：「东卤场的？」是的，往回赶；不是的，搜身。刀客头目说他们拿的是东卤场管头的钱，「场里的人一个也不许出去」。

There's only one way east that holds: a strip of hard salt crust with soft mud on either side that swallows a leg to the knee. A band of hired swordsmen guards its mouth and asks everyone, 'From the East Brine Works?' If yes, you're driven back; if not, you're searched. Their leader says they're paid by the foreman of the works: 'Not one of his people gets out.'
after: 刀客收了刀，说实话：管头手里攥着全场盐工的卖身契，契上写十年，到期了再续，没人能走。卤大的契也在里头，「那汉子每天中午爬上晒盐的高架，冲西边挥手，管头骂他偷懒，他说他在给闺女报平安」。

The swordsmen sheathe their blades and talk straight: the foreman holds every salt worker's indenture, ten years each and renewed when it runs out, so no one ever leaves. Luda's is in the pile too. 'That fellow climbs the drying frame every noon and waves toward the west. The foreman calls it shirking. He says he's letting his girl know he's well.'

name: 七色盐摊
Seven-Colour Salt Stall
before: 岔路尽头一个盐摊，摊上的盐不止白的：粉的、红的、黄的、灰的，一碗一色，像打翻了颜料。卖盐的是个泼辣的盐婆，盐好价贱，抢了盐枭的生意。一伙盐枭砸了她的摊子，拿蜃兵守着摊前，见有人来买就赶，盐婆叉着腰骂了一早上，嗓子都哑了。

At the end of a side track, a salt stall where the salt isn't only white: pink, red, yellow, grey, a bowl of each, like spilled paint. The seller is a fiery salt woman whose good, cheap salt has stolen the smugglers' trade. A gang of them smashed her stall and set mirage soldiers in front of it to drive buyers away, and she has stood with hands on hips cursing them all morning until her voice is gone.
after: 盐枭被打跑，盐婆重新摆好碗，佩服你们，开张换货。她说粉的红的是卤池里长的小东西染的，池子越咸越红；她会认，是卤大教的：「那人看一眼池子的颜色，就知道哪天收盐。」她多抓了一把粉盐塞给卤妹：「给你爹带去，他爱吃这个。」

The smugglers run, the salt woman sets her bowls out again and, impressed, opens for trade. The pinks and reds come from tiny living things in the brine pools, she says; the saltier the pool, the redder. Luda taught her to read them: 'One look at a pool's colour and he'd know which day to rake.' She tucks an extra handful of pink salt into Lumei's hands. 'Take that to your father. He loves it.'

name: 鸭栏渡
Duck-Pen Ferry
before: 咸水湖收窄的地方有个小渡口，渡口边圈着几百只鸭子，嘎嘎声震天。一伙海盗占了渡口养鸭，拿两个蜃兵插在栏边当稻草人，过渡的人要先替他们赶一圈鸭子。赶鸭的小哥被海盗支使得满头大汗，鸭子一群群往湖里跑。

Where the salt lake narrows there's a little ferry landing ringed with pens holding hundreds of ducks, quacking fit to deafen. A pirate band has taken it over to raise ducks, stuck two mirage soldiers by the pens as scarecrows, and makes anyone crossing first herd the ducks round once. The duck boy is run ragged and the ducks keep breaking for the lake.
after: 海盗被打落水，渡船又能走了。赶鸭小哥说这些鸭子是东卤场管头订的，每月送一回给他办席。他去送鸭时见过卤大：「管头吃鸭，盐工喝卤汤。上个月那汉子跟管头说，契满了他要走，管头说契丢了。」

The pirates go into the lake and the ferry runs again. The duck boy says these ducks are ordered by the East Brine Works foreman, a delivery a month for his feasts. He's seen Luda on his runs. 'The foreman eats duck and the workers drink brine soup. Last month that fellow told the foreman his contract was up and he was leaving. The foreman said the contract was lost.'

name: 盐柱林
Salt Pillar Wood
before: 沙地里立着一片盐柱，一人多高，白森森的，像一片没叶子的树林，风一吹，呜呜地响。一伙海盗在盐柱里挖了洞藏身，见人就从柱子后头扑出来。他们在柱子之间拴满了绳，绳上挂着铃铛，谁一碰，满林都响，海盗就顺着铃声围过去。

A stand of salt pillars rises from the sand, taller than a man, bone white, like a wood with no leaves, moaning when the wind blows through. A pirate band has dug hollows in them to hide, leaping out from behind pillars at anyone passing. They've strung ropes hung with bells between the pillars; touch one and the whole wood rings, and the pirates close in on the sound.
after: 海盗被赶出了盐柱林。傍晚爬到最高的一根盐柱上往东看，天上没有楼，地上远远一片白垛，一座晒盐的高架立在当中，小得像一根火柴。卤妹看了很久，没敲，也没记，只说：「这回不是天上的。」

The pirates are driven out of the pillar wood. At dusk you climb the tallest pillar and look east. There are no towers in the sky; far off on the ground lies a field of white heaps with a drying frame standing in the middle, small as a matchstick. Lumei looks for a long time. She doesn't knock and doesn't write. She only says, 'This time it isn't in the sky.'

name: 盐丁营
Salt Guard Camp
before: 东卤场外头扎着一座大营，营墙是拿盐砖垒的，太阳一照白得刺眼。管头养的盐丁里外三层，又花钱请了一营蜃兵蜃骑站在墙头充数，远看人山人海，近看一半是影子。营门挂着一块牌子：「场内盐工，契未满者，不得出营。」

Outside the East Brine Works sprawls a great camp, its walls built of salt bricks that glare white in the sun. The foreman's salt guards stand three deep inside and out, and he's paid for a troop of mirage soldiers and riders to pad out the walls, so from afar it's a sea of men and up close half of them are shadows. A board hangs on the gate: 'Salt workers whose contracts are not complete may not leave the camp.'
after: 盐丁营被打破，影子散了，真人跑了。营里的盐工围上来，听说卤妹是谁，个个笑：「你就是那个分不清真假的丫头？」他们管卤大叫「挥手的」，每天中午他在高架上挥手，大家跟着他往西看，看了三年，也学会了想家。

The camp falls, the shadows scatter and the real men run. The salt workers crowd round and, hearing who Lumei is, all start grinning. 'So you're the girl who can't tell what's real?' They call Luda 'the Waver': every noon he waves from the drying frame and they all look west with him, and in three years they've all learned to miss home.

name: 契房
Contract House
before: 盐场门口一座小砖房，铁门铁窗，是管头的契房，全场盐工的卖身契都锁在里头。管头本人缩在房里，门外剩下最后一伙盐丁和雇来的海盗守着。他隔着窗喊：「契丢了！一张也找不着！」可窗缝里分明露着一角发黄的纸。

At the gate of the salt works stands a little brick house with iron doors and iron shutters: the foreman's contract house, where every worker's indenture is locked away. The foreman himself is cowering inside, his last salt guards and hired pirates outside the door. He shouts through the shutter: 'The contracts are lost! I can't find a single one!' A corner of yellowed paper is plainly sticking out through the crack.
after: 盐丁和海盗都败了，铁门卸下来，契纸一摞摞堆在桌上，管头抱着头蹲在墙角。卤妹在里头翻出她爹那一张，契早满了两年，被人拿墨改了日子。盐工们把契纸全抱到场院里，一把火烧了，火光里有人唱起了晒盐的号子。

The guards and pirates are beaten, the iron door comes off, and the contracts lie in stacks on the table while the foreman squats in a corner with his head in his hands. Lumei finds her father's among them: it ran out two years ago, and someone has inked over the date. The salt workers carry every contract out into the yard and burn the lot, and in the firelight someone starts the salt rakers' work chant.

name: 东卤场
East Brine Works
before: 盐场正中立着那座晒盐的高架，架下是一垛垛白盐，像一座白城。盐场的伙房和粮仓还被管头最后一拨打手占着，锅里炖着鸭子，盐工们端着卤汤站在外头。正午，高架上爬上去一个人，扛着盐耙，冲西边挥手。卤妹拿起勺子，又放下了，一句话也说不出来。

In the middle of the works stands the drying frame, and beneath it heap after heap of white salt, like a white city. The works' kitchen and granary are still held by the foreman's last pack of bruisers, duck stewing in their pot while the salt workers stand outside holding bowls of brine soup. At noon a man climbs the frame with a salt rake on his shoulder and waves toward the west. Lumei lifts her spoon, lowers it again, and can't say a word.
after: 卤大爬下来抱住女儿，她拿勺子敲他，咚。他说：「海面冷，贴海的气又冷又重，上头压着暖气，远处的光在两层中间被压弯，天边背后的东西也被搬上了天。白城就是这片盐垛。」又指东北：「十年前我见过五条船倒挂在天上，往冷水去，蜃楼的光都是那儿借的。」

Luda climbs down from the frame and wraps his daughter in his arms, and she knocks him once with her spoon. Knock. 'The sea's cold,' Luda says, 'so the air lying on it is cold and heavy, with warm air pressing on top. Light from far off gets bent between the two layers, and things behind the horizon get lifted into the sky. The White City was these salt heaps.' Then he points north-east. 'Ten years ago I saw five ships hanging upside down in the sky, heading north-east toward the cold water. All the Mirage's light is borrowed from over there.'
first: 伙房和粮仓里抄出管头囤的三十只腌鸭、五十石白米、两坛好酒、一箱新棉袄，还有一筐盐工们被扣下的家信，封口都没拆。

From the kitchen and granary you seize the foreman's hoard: thirty salted ducks, fifty piculs of white rice, two jars of good wine, a chest of new padded jackets, and a basket of the workers' letters from home that he'd held back, seals still unbroken.
pass: 每次路过，东卤场的盐工都往车上搬几袋新盐，卤大再塞一包粉盐，卤妹站在高架上冲你们挥手，说：「我敲过了，你们是真的，路上别怕。」

Each time you pass, the East Brine Works hands you a few sacks of fresh salt and Luda slips in a packet of pink salt, while Lumei stands on the drying frame waving. 'I've knocked on you already. You're real. Don't be afraid on the road.'

name: 估货滩
Price-Tag Beach
before: 海边一片滩，每天清早，东边海上浮出一座集市，旗幡招展，人声隐约。集市散了，就有几个渔户划着小船从那个方向回来，船上装着布匹、铁锅、茶包。一伙海盗守在滩头，专截这些回来的小船，货抢了，人推下水。

A beach on the coast where, every morning, a market floats up on the sea to the east, banners streaming, voices faint. When it fades a few fishermen row back from that direction, their boats loaded with cloth, iron pots, packets of tea. A pirate band holds the head of the beach and waylays these returning boats, taking the goods and shoving the people overboard.
after: 海盗被赶跑，渔户们捞起了自己的货。每件货上都系着一张价签，墨色发黄，日子写着「丁未年八月廿五」，价钱是十年前的价钱。渔户说：「海市的货是真的，卖货的是假的。价签上写多少，就付多少。」

The pirates are chased off and the fishermen haul their goods back aboard. Every item has a price tag tied to it, the ink gone yellow, dated 'Dingwei year, eighth month, twenty-fifth day', priced at ten-year-old prices. 'The sea market's goods are real,' a fisherman says. 'The sellers aren't. Whatever the tag says, that's what you pay.'

name: 市牌岗
Market-Board Rise
before: 岸边高岗上立着一块旧木牌，上书「海市，辰开午散」，木牌底下坐着一个老牙郎，膝上搁一杆秤，人称老秤。每天辰时海市一出，他就对着海上的集市报价，岸上的人照他的价买卖。一伙海盗上了岗，要他报个「海盗价」，他眯着眼，一个字不改。

On a rise above the shore stands an old board reading 'Sea Market, opens at the hour of the Dragon, closes at noon', and beneath it sits an old broker with a steelyard across his knees, known as Old Scale. Every morning when the market appears he calls its prices out over the water, and the people ashore trade by his word. A pirate band has come up the rise to make him call 'pirate prices', and he squints at them and won't change a figure.
after: 海盗被打下了岗。老秤说，海市上的人他天天见，十年了，一个也没老，天天讲同样的价，买同样的东西：「那是丁未年八月廿五的集，那一天，千里号的人来赶过集。」他磕了磕秤杆：「海上的人在过那一天，岸上的人在过日子。」

The pirates are thrown off the rise. Old Scale says he's seen the people of the sea market every day for ten years and not one has aged; every day they quote the same prices and buy the same things. 'That's the market of the twenty-fifth day of the eighth month, Dingwei year. The day the Qianli's people came to market.' He taps his steelyard. 'The people out there are living that one day. The people on shore are just living.'

name: 断缆湾
Cut-Cable Cove
before: 一道湾里横七竖八拴着几十条小船，缆绳都被砍断了一半。这是一伙海盗的大营：十年里不知多少人想划船去海市，海盗就在湾口截船，人扣下做苦力，船拴在湾里。营里海盗不少，还掺着一队蜃兵，刀枪在晨光里一闪一闪。

In a cove dozens of small boats are tied every which way, their cables half hacked through. This is a pirate band's main camp: over ten years who knows how many people have tried to row out to the sea market, and the pirates catch them at the cove's mouth, keep the people as labourers and tie up the boats. There are plenty of pirates here, with a squad of mirage soldiers among them, blades glinting in the morning light.
after: 海盗营被打散，扣下的人放了。海盗头目说他自己也划去过海市，划了一整天，集市还在那么远。阿舟站在湾口看了一早上的海市，忽然指着一个人影：一个胖厨子，挑着两筐咸鱼讨价还价。「是老鼎，千里号的大厨。我小时候见过他。」

The pirate camp is broken and the captives freed. The pirate chief says he rowed for the market himself once; a whole day of rowing and it stayed just as far. A Zhou stands at the cove's mouth watching the market all morning and suddenly points at a figure: a fat cook with two baskets of salt fish, haggling. 'That's Old Ding, the Qianli's head cook. I saw him when I was a boy.'

name: 秤家栈
Scale Family Inn
before: 海边大路上一座客栈，是老秤的老伴秤婆开的，每天辰时，客人都搬了凳子坐在门口看海市，像看戏。一伙海盗占了客栈，把看海市的凳子收了钱，一张凳子一钱银子，米缸、酒坛全搬进了他们住的上房。秤婆在灶下烧火，一边烧一边骂。

A coaching inn on the coast road, run by Old Scale's wife, Granny Scale. Every morning at the hour of the Dragon the guests carry stools out to the door and watch the sea market like a play. A pirate band has taken the inn and now charges a mace of silver per stool, and the rice jars and wine jars have all gone up to the best rooms where they sleep. Granny Scale tends the stove and curses as she stokes.
after: 海盗被撵走，凳子又搬回了门口，不收钱。秤婆说十年前那一天千里号的人也住过这店，第二天一早走，今天的海市里也有他们早上出门的样子，「我天天看他们走，一回都没赶上留饭」。

The pirates are thrown out and the stools go back by the door, free of charge. Granny Scale says the Qianli's people stayed here that day ten years ago and left early next morning, and today's sea market shows them heading out that morning too. 'I watch them go every day. Never once in time to keep them breakfast.'
first: 上房里抄出海盗囤的二十坛老酒、一缸咸鱼、四袋白面，还有一摞看凳子收的碎银，秤婆数了数，正好够把被砸的窗子都换新。

From the best rooms you seize the pirates' stores: twenty jars of aged wine, a crock of salt fish, four sacks of white flour, and a pile of silver scraps from the stool fees. Granny Scale counts it: exactly enough to replace every smashed window.
pass: 每次路过，秤婆都给你们留一锅热粥、一笼包子，说：「海上那些人我留不住，你们我留得住。吃饱了再走。」
Each time you pass, Granny Scale keeps a pot of hot congee and a steamer of buns for you. 'The ones out on the sea I can't keep. You I can. Eat your fill before you go.'

name: 复日城
Same-Day Town
before: 退潮时，海边露出一道沙脊，通到一座小城，城门上写着「蜃港」。城里人来人往，热闹得很，可每个人说的话都一样：卖鱼的喊「八月廿五，新鲜的」，老头在门口说「千里号的人进城了」。几个镇丁拦住你们，递来一张纸：「你们是千里号的，照着念。」城楼上站着一个腰挂短刀的女人，正朝海上指着什么。

At low tide a sand ridge rises from the sea and leads to a small walled town, its gate reading 'Mirage Harbour'. The streets bustle, but everyone says the same things: the fishmonger calls 'Twenty-fifth of the eighth month, fresh today!', an old man at his door says 'The Qianli's people have come to town.' A few town wardens stop you and hand you a sheet of paper: 'You're the Qianli's people. Read your lines.' On the gate tower stands a woman with a short blade at her waist, pointing at something out to sea.
after: 镇丁被打退，城里人愣了一下，又接着念自己的词。城楼上那个女人的影子一晃就淡了：是海市里映出来的沈渡，十年前那一天的她。一个卖糖的老汉偷偷告诉你们：城里的人是真的，蜃港早就败了，大家照着天上那一天过日子，「那一天，人人都有钱赚」。

The wardens are driven back. The townsfolk falter for a moment, then go on with their lines. The woman on the gate tower wavers and fades: Shen Du, cast up by the sea market as she was that day ten years ago. An old sweet seller whispers that the townsfolk are real. Mirage Harbour fell on hard times long ago, and everyone lives by that one day in the sky. 'On that day, everyone made money.'

name: 抽水礁
Skim Reef
before: 海市底下有一片礁，退潮时露出来，岸上几个还在做买卖的渔户就在礁上摆摊，对着天上的集市照价收货。一伙海盗盘踞礁头，每卖一样抽三成，叫「抽水」，还拉着一队蜃弓手站在礁顶，远看像一座炮台。渔户们挤在礁脚，货摊挨着海浪。

Beneath the sea market lies a reef that shows at low tide, and the few fishermen still trading ashore set up stalls on it, buying and selling by the prices in the sky. A pirate band has taken the head of the reef and skims three parts in ten from every sale, 'drawing water' they call it, with a squad of mirage archers posted on top so from afar it looks like a fort. The fishermen are crowded at the reef's foot, stalls lapped by waves.
after: 海盗被赶下了礁，渔户的摊子挪回了好地方。一个老渔户望着天上的集市叹气：「五年前，海市上的人脸上的麻子都数得清；现在鼻子眼睛都糊了。」他说海市一年比一年淡，像一幅晒久了的画。

The pirates are driven off the reef and the fishermen's stalls move back to the good spots. An old fisherman looks up at the market in the sky and sighs. 'Five years ago you could count the pockmarks on those people's faces. Now their noses and eyes are a blur.' The market fades a little more every year, he says, like a painting left too long in the sun.

name: 十年账楼
Ten-Year Ledger Loft
before: 荒原上一座小木楼，楼上堆满了账本，是老秤十年来的海市账：每天海市卖了什么、什么价，他都记一笔。一伙海盗听说账里记着「海市藏货的地方」，带着一队蜃骑围了木楼，在楼下堆柴，说再不交账就点火。老秤抱着一摞账本坐在楼梯口，一动不动。

A small timber loft on the plain, crammed with ledgers: Old Scale's ten years of sea-market accounts, every day's sales and prices written down. A pirate band has heard the books record 'where the sea market hides its goods' and surrounded the loft with a troop of mirage riders, piling firewood underneath and threatening to light it if he won't hand them over. Old Scale sits at the top of the stairs hugging a stack of ledgers and doesn't move.
after: 海盗被赶走，柴堆搬开了。老秤翻账给你们看：十年里每天卖的都是同样的东西，可每天的总数都比前一天少一点，第一年三百二十样，今年只剩一百一十样。「不是货少了，是天上的摊子一个个没了。」他合上账：「有人记不住那一天了。」

The pirates are run off and the firewood carried away. Old Scale shows you the ledgers: every day for ten years the same goods sold, but each day's total a little smaller than the last. Three hundred and twenty items the first year, a hundred and ten this year. 'The goods haven't run out. The stalls in the sky are going, one by one.' He shuts the book. 'Someone can't remember that day any more.'

name: 换忆摊
Memory-Swap Stall
before: 海边一座半塌的货棚，棚里堆着真东西：铜盆、绸缎、成箱的针线。看摊的却是个蜃楼里映下来的老掌柜，隔着一层水光朝你们笑，不收钱，只收一段记得清清楚楚的事：你说一件，他递一件货。说完了，你自己就记不太清了。一伙海盗守在棚前，把来换货的人一个个撵走，要独吞这笔买卖。

A half-collapsed goods shed on the shore, piled with real things: copper basins, satin, crates of needles and thread. But the stall keeper is an old merchant cast down from the Mirage, smiling at you through a sheen of water. He takes no money, only a memory you remember clearly: tell him one, and he hands you one item. Once you've told it, you can't quite remember it yourself. A pirate band guards the front of the shed and chases off everyone who comes to trade, meaning to keep the business for themselves.
after: 海盗被打跑，老掌柜照旧开张，愿意跟你们换货。小桨拿一顿难吃的晚饭换了一口铁锅，换完拍着肚子说已经想不起来哪里难吃了。阿汐想了想，没换：「我爹的事，一件也不给。」老掌柜笑着点头，像十年前也有人这么跟他说过。

The pirates are routed and the old merchant opens for business as before, happy to trade with you. Xiaojiang swaps a memory of a dreadful dinner for an iron pot, then pats his stomach and says he can't recall what was dreadful about it. Axi thinks a moment and doesn't trade. 'Nothing about my father. Not one thing.' The old merchant smiles and nods, as if someone told him the same ten years ago.
